_comment: Copy to pipeline/character/<video>/shots/<nn>-<type>.json. Written by character-shots (P1). The video block is compiled to segments/<nn>-<type>/prompt.txt. Character and world paths are relative to the handle's folder; keyframes/ is relative to the video's folder. scripts/character/shots.py validate checks it; shots.py refs writes refs.json from video.references; scripts/character/keyframes.sh renders keyframe_prompt with keyframe_references. B (a silent generated action) uses the same file: framing_kind hands_only or subject_only (face only for an approved mascot), no phone, no line, no voice reference; its action carries the plan beat's action word for word, and fixed_subjects_in_shot the beat's exact subjects. X (a silent reaction) uses the same file: framing_kind face, no phone, no line, no voice reference, and 'reaction' copied exactly from its plan beat (ref_id, framing, camera_distance, expression_beats); the PERFORMANCE section of the prompt carries each expression beat's face, eyes and head word for word with its time from the segment's start ('at 0.8 s'), states 'No lip sync' and 'She does not speak', and never names the reference post, its creator or its file. No reference of the generation is research footage or the reference clip.
segment_type: T | O | G | S | H | F | B
script_lines: <ids of the frozen script lines this segment speaks; 'demo-vo' for a demo performance>
framing: medium chest-up, phone propped at eye level, face fills most of the frame
framing_kind: face | hands_only | subject_only (who is in the picture; the keyframe's people rule)
beat_ids: <v2: the plan beats of this segment>
action: <one action, written as movement; ends in a visible state>
props: <each prop, and whose hand it is in>

phone.screen_id: <O, G, S, H, F: the row id in apps/<slug>/screens/SCREENS.md; else null>
phone.angle: flat-on: screen plane square to the lens, upright, no tilt, no perspective (hard rule)

finger.start_place: raised beside the phone, off the screen edge
finger.travel: about a third of the screen height

keyframe_prompt: <the still that opens the segment: the same person in the outfit, in the set, in the first-frame pose; for O, G, S, H, F the phone already up and flat solid green; for F the other hand already raised beside the phone. A real phone photo, no text.>
keyframe_end_prompt: <H only: the end still, the phone at its end size and flat-on; else null>
priority_order: identity from creator file and anchors
fixed subjects: count, look, true size
phone and green screen, when present

earned: <at most five, each with its row in pipeline/character/model-failures.md>

video.model: <slug in scripts/character/models.json; default minimax-h3-max-reference-to-video; the active version must match>
video.trim_to_seconds: <the planned length when it is under the model's 5 s minimum, else null>
video._references_comment: kind is one of keyframe, hero, anchor, subject, set, neighbour-frame, voice; nothing else, and never a screen. At most max_reference_images pictures in models.json (4 on the default model), the keyframe first. The voice clip is not counted. role is the binding sentence for the REFERENCES section of the prompt.

references.role: the first frame: composition, pose, set, light
the character's face and hair (characters/<character>/references/anchors/hero.png for a character that is not the handle's identity)
the voice only: tone, pitch, accent, pace

video.camera: phone propped at eye level, subtle micro-shake, no cuts
video.phone_angle: <O, G, S only, pasted as it is:> The phone is held completely flat-on to the camera: the screen plane is square to the lens and upright, with no tilt, no turn and no perspective, from the first frame to the last.

beats.delivery: <which word lifts, where it slows, the breath>

video.speech: on camera, lips in sync, eyes on the lens
keep_fixed: exactly one person (face); one person's hands (hands_only); no person (subject_only)

reaction: <X only: the plan beat's reaction, copied exactly; else omit>
